text: CPU port DDR. Protection: the original loader leaves $EF here; frame_update, room02_frame and room10_frame loop for ever when it differs.

Player whose turn it is: 0 = player 1 (joystick port 1), 1 = player 2 (port 2). show_title_screen sets 0, lose_fall flips it (EOR 1) in a two-player game. Index of room_unvisited (room*2+player), room13_band_bonus (player*4) and extra_fall_pickups_left.

Pointer (lo/hi): room palette record in irq_game_bottom (every frame), lantern record in swap_room_lanterns and advance_aux_ptr_by_4, mask column 2 in expand_contact_mask.
Pointer (lo/hi) to the raster split list of the room (from room_split_list_ptr), set and read by irq_game_bottom.
Pointer (lo/hi) to the 64-byte sprite image that copy_sprite_frame fills; set by set_sprite_buffer_pointer from sprite_buffer_addresses.
Colour RAM pointer (lo/hi) of the upper row of the map cell being drawn: draw_room starts it at $D878, room_draw_step_cell and inc_colour_ptr_top advance it, map_tile_set_black writes through it.
Colour RAM pointer (lo/hi) of the lower row of the map cell (draw_room starts it at $D8A0). Also the colour RAM row of the contact test: set_char_row_pointers sets it, check_col0/1/2_colour read it.

Pointer (lo/hi) into the lantern list of a room (from lantern_list_ptr; 4-byte records, end at a byte with bit 7 set): check_lantern_pickup, setup_room_lanterns_and_init, reset_room_lanterns, next_lantern_record.

Read pointer of random_byte: lda (random_ptr),y after INC random_ptr; frame_update also increments the low byte every frame. restart_to_title points it at random_table, but init_game_variables then clears the high byte, so the bytes come from zero page and the stack page.
24-bit busy-wait counter of show_player_screen ($18 low, $19 middle, $1A high), start value $038080, counted down to zero.

check_background_contact: (actor Y - 29) AND 7 = pixel row inside the character; build_shift_mask pads the mask with this many rows.

Read pointer (lo/hi) of the attract demo input stream: start_attract_demo and show_title_screen set it to demo_input_stream ($F300), update_actors reads one byte per pass and advances it. The title protection wipe at $06F3 writes through it. At cold start expand_frame_shape uses the low byte as its row count.

Read pointer (lo/hi) of the attract demo input stream: start_attract_demo and start_new_game set it to demo_input_stream ($F300), update_actors reads one byte per pass in the demo and advances it. title_protection_wipe writes through it. Source bits of double_pixel_nibble (expand_contact_mask): each set bit becomes a %11 multicolour pixel.
24-bit number of points (high byte first) that add_pending_score adds to score; add_score clears it and stores A at points_to_add+X.

Falls (lives) left of the current player, shown as FALLS nn: 4 at game start (9 when Yamo is player controlled), lose_fall decrements it (negative = game over), extra falls increment it. First byte of the player block $28-$43 that lose_fall swaps with inactive_player_state.
Current room 0-19 (18 = wizard, 19 = congratulations). change_room ($2F9A) copies next_room here; read by draw_room, the room init/frame dispatch and most room tables.
Current room 0-19 (18 = wizard, 19 = congratulations). change_room copies next_room here; read by draw_room, the room init/frame dispatch and most room tables.

Lanterns not yet taken, one byte per room (room_lanterns_left+room), part of the player block. reset_lantern_counts copies room_lantern_count_init; check_lantern_pickup decrements the room entry. Room code tests other rooms (e.g. room 6 opens passages in rooms 0-2 and 5).

Number of completed game loops: room19_frame increments it when the congratulations room ends and play starts again. Nonzero: both enemies come at once and faster (spawn timers, actor_recover, wake_idle_enemies) and the room 13 runner tracks are longer.
Score of the current player, 24-bit binary, high byte first ($41 high). add_pending_score adds points_to_add; score_to_bcd and update_high_score read it. Last bytes of the player block $28-$43.
Index of the next raster split line in raster_split_lines: frame_update and irq_game_playfield set 0, irq_game_colour_split increments it.
SPENA AND $1F saved by draw_room while it draws, restored at its end.

Frame countdown: every raster handler (frame_update, irq_title_frame, irq_player_screen) decrements it until 0. The main loop sets 3 and waits for 0 (one pass = 3 frames); the title, player screen and game over set it and wait.

16-bit frame countdown (lo/hi): show_title_screen sets $0960 (2400 frames), the IRQs decrement it, at 0 title_menu_loop starts the attract demo. room19_init reuses it as the length of the congratulations room (room19_frame).
Key code AND $7F of the last game key (handle_game_keys); pause_debounce and reset_play_state store $FF. Nothing reads it.

Scratch: bit shifter of the collision scan in check_fight_collisions, loop counter of check_tile_row, slider index 2..0 in room17_frame; act_wall_bump_undo_again stores the facing here.

animate_scrolling_chars: 0 = phase counts up, 1 = down; flipped after each speed cycle. draw_room and room frame handlers set it; actor_continue_action moves a climbing actor down when nonzero.

Per actor: Y position (sprite Y = value + $1D), limits $2E-$C6.
Per actor: 0 = facing left, 1 = facing right.

Per actor, state $17 (ride): steps until the next move (4 after a move).

Per actor: sprites of other actors it touches this pass (bit 1 Bruce, bit 3 Yamo, bit 4 Ninja), built by check_fight_collisions.

Per actor: action state of the state machine (actor_action_step, actor_set_state*, actor_continue_action); $17 climbing, $18 wall bump, $19 hazard death, $1A ducking.

Per actor: frame width of the overlay sprite, 0 = 8 pixels, else 16.

Per actor: collision code (3-7) of its first sprite, from actor_collision_code_first (spawn_actor); remove_actor frees its sprite slot.

Per actor: collision code of its second sprite, 0 = none (actor_collision_code_second).

256 random bytes from SID voice 3 noise, made by cold_start. random_byte does not read it (random_ptr high byte is 0 in play).

Zero bytes, never read or written.

charsets $A000-$B7FF (they would be garbage). Nothing in the program writes it; the image holds 0.
must be 0

Cold start (program entry). Runs once after loading.
- Blanks the screen and sets the stack.
- When $03FF is zero (always in this image): fills page $0200 with 256 random bytes from SID voice 3
  noise, copies the first 512 bytes of the character ROM to $8800-$89FF with inverted copies at
  $8A00-$8BFF (the hires text font of the title menu and the status line), patches three characters
  of that font, and expands the font sources $9000/$9400/$9800 into charsets.
- Always expands the font source $9C00, runs the protection wait and sprite pre-shift at $512F,
  sets the memory configuration to RAM + I/O and the fixed sprite colours, then falls into
  restart_to_title.
Each font source holds 128 characters of 8 bytes. The expansion routine at $4892 doubles every
pixel row: rows 0-3 of character n become character n of the first output charset (top half) and
rows 4-7 become character n+128 (bottom half). The four sources give the 2 KB charsets at $A000
(rooms 0-9), $A800 (rooms 10-17 and 19), $B000 (room 18, the wizard) and $B800.

Cold start (program entry). Runs once after loading.
- Disables interrupts, sets the stack and blanks the screen.
- When warm_start_flag is 0 (always in this image): fills random_table with 256 bytes of SID voice 3
  noise, copies characters 0-63 of the character ROM into text_font ($8800-$89FF) with inverted copies in
  text_font_inverse ($8A00-$8BFF) (the hires font of the title menu and the status line), patches three
  characters of that font, and expands room_charset_a/b/c into charset_rooms_0_9, charset_rooms_10_19 and
  charset_wizard.
- Always expands room_charset_d into charset_wizard_flash, calls build_contact_masks (protection wait on

Draw the current room ($29) and reset the per-room state. Called at a room change ($2FCC), at the
start of a game and of the demo. Screen and sprites are off while it draws.
1. Clears status row 0 and fills colour RAM of rows 3-24 with the room colour ($47A0 + room).
2. Room 11 when the lanterns of rooms 12, 14 and 16 are all taken: goes to room 13 instead.
3. First visit of the room by the current player ($0300 + room*2 + player = 1): clears the flag
   and adds 2000 points ($07D0).
4. Clears the room object state ($4F57-$4FDA), the room timer $87/$88, $65; sets $4321 = 7.
5. Loads the spawn timers: Ninja $5D from $130B, Yamo $5E from $1347 (3 for both after the first
   completed game, 8 for Yamo when player 2 controls him); $7A = $4C9E (no enemies in the room).
6. Resets fields of Bruce, copies the room's 20-byte record from $4AA8 to $0153 and selects the
   charset ($F2): $A000 for rooms 0-9, $B000 for room 18, $A800 for the others.
7. Decodes the run-length room map (pointer $4B34/$4B49 + room) into screen rows 3-24.
8. Draws the lanterns ($336E), turns the screen and the sprites 0-4 on and tail-jumps to the
   per-room init at $3A6F.
Map format: a stream of codes. $80 ends the map. $81-$FF: (code & $7F) literal tile bytes
follow. $01-$7F: one tile byte follows, repeated code times. A tile byte draws one double-height
cell: bits 0-6 = character c (top row c, bottom row c+128), bit 7 = draw the cell with colour
RAM $F8 (multicolour, colour 0) instead of the room colour. Cells fill 40 columns, then the
next double row.
screen off

Draw the current room and reset the per-room state. Called by change_room, start_new_game and
start_attract_demo. Screen and sprites are off while it draws.
1. Clears status row 0, fills colour RAM rows 3-24 with room_colour_fill[room], clears the fireball
   sprites and silences the sound effects.
2. Room 11 when room_lanterns_left of rooms 12, 14 and 16 are all 0: goes to room 13 instead
   (place_bruce_at_room_start with X = 13).
3. First visit of the room by the current player (room_unvisited[room*2 + current_player] = 1): clears the
   flag and adds 2000 points.
4. Clears actor_move_queue (the move history of the actors, $4F57-$4FDA), room_time and
   anim_chars_direction; anim_chars_speed_step = 7.
5. room_no_enemy_flag = room_no_enemies[room] (nonzero also clears enemy_follow_x). Loads the spawn timers
   from ninja_room_delay / yamo_room_delay (3 for both when game_loop_count is nonzero, Yamo 8 when player 2
   controls him).

Prints message A (pointer table at $43BE) on text row X at offset Y from the row start.
Text row 0 = screen row 0, row 1 = screen row 1, row n >= 2 = screen rows 2n-1 and 2n
(table $4338/$434C, built by $0869). Each message byte b gives glyph g = b - $20: g AND $7F
goes to the upper screen row and g OR $80 to the lower row, so text is two rows high. Byte
$A0 ends the message. When $0100 <> 0 the lower row goes to $DE00 (ignored), so the text
is one row high. Rows 0 and 1 are always one row high. Uses $04-$09. Changes A, X, Y.

Print message A (pointer table message_ptrs) on text row X at offset Y from the row start.
Text row 0 = screen row 0, row 1 = screen row 1, row n >= 2 = screen rows 2n-1 and 2n (text_line_top_lo/hi

State: $BF,X action state, $CE,X action timer (steps left), $0106,X step delay (passes to skip).
  1. If the step delay is nonzero, count it down and return.
  2. Push the move record of the last step into the move history ($4F57, 11 records of
     up/down/left/right counts per actor) and clear the current record.
  3. Count how long the state has stayed the same ($CB,X, 6 down to 0).
  4. Wall bump: when the terrain flags $B6,X have bit 3 (inside a wall), undo the moves of the
     last step and enter state $18.
  5. A nonzero timer continues the current timed action (actor_continue_action, Y = timer).
  6. A zero timer starts a new action from the joystick: direction $98,X, fire $9B,X.

Plays sound $80 at the start of a walk, climb or jump. Keeps A, X and Y.
It also hides two copy-protection checks on bytes of the protection page $CF00:
  1. $1166 (= $CF79 EOR $CF99, set at $0CDE). When zero, it increments the operands of the
     instructions at $0CD8 so the next game start compares the next byte pair; when the operand
     reaches $99 it writes $9A (TXS) over the first instruction of the routine at $1159.
  2. protection_check_value (= $CF7A EOR $CF9A, set by the main loop). When zero, it increments the
     operands of main_loop_protection_check; when the operand reaches $9A it writes $9A (TXS)
     over the CLC at step_sound_crash_point, with X = 4, so the stack pointer becomes $04 and the
     following PLA/RTS crash the game.
With the original protection bytes both values are nonzero and nothing happens.

Builds the sprite images of the three actors for the next frame (main loop, and once after a room change).
Actor 0 is Bruce (sprites 0+1), actor 1 is Yamo (sprites 2+3), actor 2 is the Ninja (sprite 4 only).
For each active actor ($95,x bit 0) it copies the frame $4f4e,x into the main sprite and frame $4f4e,x+1
into the overlay sprite, in the sprite buffer that sprite_buffer_select does not show now.
It also stores the width flag ($d4,x/$d7,x), the colour ($da,x/$dd,x) and the height ($e0,x) of the frames.
At the end it clears sprite_images_shown, so the raster interrupt shows the new images (show_actor_sprites).

Fight collision check, once per main loop frame (skipped in rooms where $4c9e,room <> 0).
Reads the VIC-II sprite-sprite collision register $d01e (reading clears it). Bits $03 count as Bruce,
$0c as Yamo, $30 as the Ninja. For each pair of actors that touch, $b3,x of each actor gets the bit of the
other actor's sprite: bit 1 = Bruce (sprite 1), bit 3 = Yamo (sprite 3), bit 4 = Ninja (sprite 4).
Then each actor X is tested as the victim of each actor Y it touches (check_fight_pair):
a hit needs the attacker in an attack state and the victim in front of it (check_attack_reach).
A hit sets $bc,y bit 0 (attacker landed a hit) and on the victim $bc,x bit 1 (enemy strike),
bit 2 (punch), bit 3 (flying kick) or bit 4 (fall attack), plus bit 7 when the attacker is Bruce.
Then it continues in apply_fight_hits. $b3-$b5 and $bc-$be are cleared first.

Fight collision check, once per main loop pass (the main loop skips it in rooms whose room_no_enemies entry
is nonzero). Reads SPSPCL (sprite-sprite collisions; the read clears it) into sprite_collisions. Bits $03 count
as Bruce, $0C as Yamo, $30 as the Ninja. For each pair of actors that touch, actor_touch_mask,X of each gets the
bit of the other actor's sprite: bit 1 = Bruce (sprite 1), bit 3 = Yamo (sprite 3), bit 4 = Ninja (sprite 4).
Then each actor X is tested as the victim of each actor Y it touches (check_fight_pair): a hit needs the
attacker in an attack state and the victim in front of it (check_attack_reach).
A hit sets actor_hit_flags,Y bit 0 (attacker landed a hit) and on the victim actor_hit_flags,X bit 1 (Ninja
strike), bit 2 (punch), bit 3 (flying kick) or bit 4 (fall attack), plus bit 7 when the attacker is Bruce.
Then it continues in apply_fight_hits. actor_touch_mask and actor_hit_flags are cleared first.

($a4,y = 1), else attacker X - victim X. Compares A with the reach in $61. Returns carry set and N clear
when the victim is in front of the attacker at a distance of reach or more.

Animates the background characters $61, $62 and $63 by rotating 8-byte patterns. Called by the room
code of rooms 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 11. $60 is a frame delay: when it counts to 0, the patterns move one row
(animate_scrolling_chars_step). Bit 7 of $60 is a pause of (value and $7f) frames.
The delays come from $4cb2 indexed by $4321 (7 down to 0: 8, 6, 4, 2, 4, 6, 8 frames, then a pause

Message pointer table: 101 words, index = message number (A of print_message $17E2). print_message points

Message format: one byte per cell, ended by $A0. Cell code = (byte - $20) AND $7F; the top half goes to the
top row of the text line, code OR $80 (the bottom half of the double-height font) to the bottom row.
So ASCII letters, digits and punctuation print as text, and the other bytes select graphic characters.

Raster band palettes: 3-byte records (BGCOL0, BGCOL1, BGCOL2), one record per colour band, band 0 first.
room_palette_ptr points each room at its first record; irq_game_bottom copies 12 bytes from there to
room_band_colours every frame. A room uses 1 + (number of raster splits) records, so the copied bytes after
them are not used.

Raster lines of the colour splits of the current room (4 bytes, ended by $FD), copied each frame by

Raster lines of the colour splits of the current room (4 bytes, ended by $FD), copied every frame by

Raster split lists: raster lines where the next colour band starts (the colours change 3 lines later),
ended by $FD. $FD is also the raster line of irq_game_bottom. split_list_none = no split.
Per-room pointer (20 words, index = room) to the room's band palette records.
Per-room pointer (20 words, index = room) to the room's raster split list.

Room drawer: called after each map cell. Counts the column counter $F3 down; when it passes 0 it reloads 39
and adds 40 to the four pointers $04 (top row), $08 (bottom row), $10 and $12 (their colour RAM rows), so the
next cell starts two screen rows lower (a map cell is a double-height character). Preserves A.

Called by draw_room after each map cell. Counts column_counter down; when it passes 0 it reloads 39 and adds
40 to row_ptr_top, row_ptr_bottom, colour_ptr_top and colour_ptr_bottom, so the next cell starts two screen rows
lower (a map cell is a double-height character and the per-cell increments have already crossed one row).
Preserves A, X, Y.
column counter

39: 40 cells per row (counts 39..0)

Builds a double-height charset from an 8x8 font. Input: $04 = source (128 chars of 8 bytes), $06 = output
for the top halves, $08 = output for the bottom halves, $F3 = number of chars - 1 ($7F).
For each source char, rows 0-3 are written twice each to ($06) and rows 4-7 twice each to ($08), so char c
of the output charset is the top half and char c+$80 the bottom half of source char c. The cold start calls it
4 times ($9000->$A000/$A400, $9400->$A800/$AC00, $9800->$B000/$B400, $9C00->$B800/$BC00).

Builds a double-height charset from an 8x8 font. Input: row_ptr_top = source (128 chars of 8 bytes), data_ptr =
output for the top halves, row_ptr_bottom = output for the bottom halves, column_counter = number of chars - 1
($7F). For each source char, rows 0-3 are written twice each to (data_ptr) and rows 4-7 twice each to
(row_ptr_bottom), so char c of the output charset is the top half and char c+$80 the bottom half of source char
c. cold_start calls it 4 times: room_charset_a -> charset_rooms_0_9, room_charset_b -> charset_rooms_10_19,
room_charset_c -> charset_wizard, room_charset_d -> charset_wizard_flash (top halves at +0, bottom at +$400).
Rows 0-3: each source row twice into the top-half char.
Rows 4-7: each source row twice into the bottom-half char.
next char

Sets up the status line for the top of the next frame (screen $8C00 with the status font at $8800, BGCOL0
grey), arms irq_game_playfield at raster $40, copies the room's 12-byte band palette to $0153-$015E and its
split list to raster_split_lines, then runs the per-frame work $15A8 (music, timers, ...) and returns.
Chain: irq_game_bottom -> irq_game_playfield (line $40) -> irq_game_colour_split for each line in
raster_split_lines -> irq_game_bottom (line $FD).
D018: screen $8C00, charset $8800

Sets up the status line for the top of the next frame (game_screen with text_font, BGCOL0 grey), arms
irq_game_playfield at raster $40, copies the room's 12-byte band palette to room_band_colours and its split
list to raster_split_lines, then runs the per-frame work frame_update (sound effects, timers, joysticks, ...)
and returns from the interrupt.
Chain: irq_game_bottom -> irq_game_playfield (line $40) -> irq_game_colour_split for each line in
raster_split_lines -> irq_game_bottom (line $FD).
D018 $32: screen $8C00 (game_screen), charset $8800 (text_font)

Game raster IRQ at line $40 (top of the playfield). Waits until the raster passes $41 and a short delay, then
switches to the room font ($F2 -> VMCSB) and band 0 colours ($0153-$0155), resets the split index $44 = 0 and
the palette offset $F4 = 3, and arms the first split.

Game raster IRQ at line $40 (top of the playfield). Waits until the raster passes $41 plus a short delay, then
switches to the room font (room_vmcsb -> VMCSB) and the band 0 colours (room_band_colours+0..2), sets
raster_split_index = 0 and band_palette_offset = 3, and arms the first split.
room font (D018 value)

Arms the next IRQ at raster_split_lines[$44]. A value of $FD ends the list: then the vector goes back to
irq_game_bottom (which runs at that same line $FD).

Arms the next IRQ at raster_split_lines[raster_split_index]. A value of $FD ends the list: then the vector goes
back to irq_game_bottom (which runs at that same line $FD).

Game raster IRQ at a split line r. Loads the next band colours ($0153+$F4.. $0155+$F4), waits for raster line
r+3 (or r+2 plus a delay, to stay in step) and writes BGCOL0-BGCOL2 at once. Then $F4 += 3, $44 += 1 and the next
split (or irq_game_bottom) is armed.

Game raster IRQ at a split line r. Loads the next band colours (room_band_colours + band_palette_offset, 3 bytes),
waits for raster line r+3 (or r+2 plus a delay) and writes BGCOL0-BGCOL2 together. Then band_palette_offset
+= 3, raster_split_index += 1 and the next split (or irq_game_bottom) is armed.
A = r+2
X = r+3

Title screen logo: four rows of 40 character codes, written OR $80 by $0626 to screen rows 5 ($8CC8),
6 ($8CF0), 2 ($8C50) and 9 ($8D68).

Title screen logo: four rows of 40 character codes that show_title_screen (title_copy_logo_rows) writes OR $80

row 6 ($8CF0, BRUCE LEE bottom half), row 2 ($8C50, DATASOFT PRESENTS) and row 9 ($8D68, BY RON J FORTIER).

Big "PLAYER n" banner shown at a game start ($0EEB, rows 7-8) and at a player change ($1918, rows 5-6):

Big "PLAYER n" text, 16 character codes for the top row and 16 for the bottom row, written OR $80. Shown by

Bytes 14-15 of each row hold the digit: both copy it there from player_banner_digit_top/bottom with index
current_player*2 (game_over copies only byte 14; its loop ends after one pass).
Top-row codes of the digits "1" (bytes 0-1) and "2" (bytes 2-3) of the player banner.
Bottom-row codes of the digits "1" and "2" of the player banner.

Joystick rotation for the rotated (handedness) mode of $16A9: new = (joy >> 2) OR joy_rotate_bits[joy AND 3].
Up -> right, down -> left, left -> up, right -> down (CIA bits 0-3 = up, down, left, right).

Joystick rotation for the left-handed mode of frame_update (joystick_right_handed = 0):
new = (joy >> 2) OR joy_rotate_bits[joy AND 3]. CIA bits 0-3 = up, down, left, right, 0 = pressed.
Result: up -> right, down -> left, left -> up, right -> down.

Room 18: Bruce X ($9E) limits of the wizard face zones. $3D42 compares with entries 2 and 1 ($76, $3A):
X >= $76 -> zone 2, X >= $3A -> zone 1, else zone 0 (entry 0 is not compared). The zone selects the face
messages $38+zone, $3B+zone, $3E+zone.

Room 18: Bruce X (actor_x) limits of the wizard face zones. room18_frame compares with entries 2 and 1
($76, $3A): X >= $76 -> zone 2, X >= $3A -> zone 1, else zone 0 (entry 0 is not compared). The zone selects the
face messages $38+zone, $3B+zone and $3E+zone.

Frames to hold each character state: 28 bytes indexed by the state number ($BF,x). The state setters
($1F92, $1FA0, $1FAE, $24F4) copy the entry to the delay counter $0106,x; $1C5B skips the character update

Step delay of each actor state: 28 bytes indexed by the state number (actor_state). The state setters
(actor_set_state, actor_set_state_timer15, actor_set_state_timer12, actor_continue_state and the hit state
setter) copy the entry to actor_step_delay,x; actor_action_step skips that many main loop passes before the

Per-room pointer (20 words) to a 20-byte block that the room drawer ($0A83) copies to $0153-$0166.
irq_game_bottom overwrites $0153-$015E every frame and no code reads $015F-$0166, so the blocks have no effect.

Per-room pointer (20 words) to a 20-byte block that draw_room copies to room_band_colours ($0153-$0166).
irq_game_bottom overwrites $0153-$015E every frame and no code reads $015F-$0166, so the blocks have no effect.
Room aux blocks: groups of 5 bytes. A block runs into the next ones (each copy is 20 bytes).

Room map addresses, low bytes then high bytes (21 entries: rooms 0-19 and the end of the last map $7FE0).
The room drawer ($0AAF) reads the map of room $29.
Map format: a byte with bit 7 clear is a run: count = byte, then one cell code drawn count times; a byte with
bit 7 set is a literal block: count = byte AND $7F (0 = end of map) cell codes follow. Each cell is a
double-height char: code on the top row, code OR $80 on the row below (codes with bit 7 set also go through
$0B5F). 40 cells per row pair (room_draw_step_cell).

Room map addresses, low bytes then high bytes (21 entries: rooms 0-19 and the end of the last map $7FE0).
draw_room reads the map of the current room.
Map format: a byte with bit 7 clear is a run: count = byte, then one cell code drawn count times; a byte with
bit 7 set is a literal block: count = byte AND $7F (0 = end of map) cell codes follow. Each cell is a
double-height char: code on the top row, code OR $80 on the row below (codes with bit 7 set also go through
map_tile_set_black). 40 cells per row pair (room_draw_step_cell).

Room exits. A character standing on exit marker char 2, 3, 4 or 5 (code AND $7F, tested by $2E89) leaves

Entry X = 0 means no exit for that marker: $2F4F falls through to the next marker's table.
exit2_dest_room: destination room per room (20 bytes).

Room exits. A character touching exit marker char 2, 3, 4 or 5 (code AND $7F, handle_touched_tile) leaves the
room through take_exit2..take_exit5: exitN_dest_room[room] = new room, exitN_entry_x/y[room] = Bruce's X/Y in
the new room. Bruce changes the room (change_room); an enemy is removed (enter_room).
Entry X = 0 means no exit for that marker: the code goes on with the next marker's tables.
exit2_dest_room: destination room per room (20 bytes).

  +0 state: 1 = lantern present, 0 = collected (game start $33CA sets all to 1)

  +2 column (Y offset in the text line), +3 text line.
$331C finds a present lantern at a column/line, clears its state, decrements $2A+room and returns the
replacement code; $336E redraws the collected lanterns when the room is drawn.

Per-room pointer to the room's lantern list (21 words: rooms 0-19 and a spare list).

  +0 state: 1 = lantern present, 0 = collected (reset_all_lanterns sets all to 1 at a game start)
  +1 replacement cell code drawn when the lantern is collected (top = AND $7F, bottom = OR $80)
  +2 column (Y offset in the text line), +3 text line.

Room init handlers: 20 words, target-1, index = room. room_init_dispatch jumps to the handler of the current

Actor workspace. A game start ($0F72) clears $4EED-$4FE7.

Actor workspace. init_game_variables clears $4EED-$4FE7 (contact_col0 .. burst_trap_row) at a game start.

Index 0-15 = a 4-bit value made of two multicolour pixel codes of a background char under set sprite pixels

Background contact tables of check_background_contact, one per mask column (23 bytes each).
Index 0-15 = a 4-bit value made of two multicolour pixel codes of a background char under set sprite pixels
(high nibble and low nibble of charset byte AND mask). A nonzero entry means the pair was seen.
Entries 16-22 hold the pairs 3, 7, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 (pairs with a %11 pixel) seen in chars whose colour RAM
colour is not 0; the swap routines move them there.

1 while the current char of mask column 0/1/2 has colour RAM colour (bits 0-2) not 0, i.e. while the %11 pairs

1 while the current char of mask column 0/1/2 has a colour RAM colour (bits 0-2) other than 0. While it is 1 the

Copy of contact_col0_lit..contact_col2_lit while the upper-body result is evaluated.

Mask row at which the upper-body result (actor_contact_upper) is taken: contact_last_row - 6.

Mask row after the last one scanned: pixel row in char (contact_pixel_y) + $15.

Cleared with the counters below; no code reads it.

Result counters of evaluate_contact: nonzero = the mask touches background pixels of code %01, %10, %11 in a

Result counters of evaluate_contact: nonzero = the mask touches background pixels of code %01, %10, %11 in a

Owner character of hardware sprites 3-7 (5 bytes, slot = $59AE[sprite - 3]); $FF = free (game start $081C,
release $3023). $0E21 writes the character index.

Owner actor of hardware sprites 0-4 (5 bytes, index = sprite number; $FF = free). set_sprite_slot_owner maps a
collision code 3-7 to its sprite through collision_code_to_sprite and stores the actor there; reset_play_state
sets all to $FF, remove_actor frees the actor's sprites, check_fight_collisions reads the owner of each sprite

Per-character count of body bumps left (3 bytes): $2B06 uses one when a character pushes into another and
does nothing when it is 0; refilled to 2 when bump_refill_timer reaches 0.

Per-actor count of fall attacks that can still hit (3 bytes): check_fight_fall uses one each time the actor
lands on another one from $0A or more above (fall attack, state $0E) and gives no hit when it is 0. frame_update
refills all three to 2 when fall_attack_refill_timer reaches 0 (every 256 frames).
Animation pose of each character (3 bytes, even number) chosen by $2780-$29A1; char_pose_b = pose + 1.

Animation pose of each actor (3 bytes, even number) chosen by select_actor_pose / set_actor_pose;
actor_pose_b = pose + 1.

Frame numbers of the two sprites of each character: pose + facing offset ($59A5 by the direction bits of
$95,x). They index the frame address tables $1167/$1239; check_background_contact uses char_frame_a.
char_pose of each character before the current pose update.
actor_pose of each actor before the current pose update.

Delayed movement queue: 11 records of 4 step counters (one per direction) x 3 characters, interleaved
(counter d of record r for character x at $4F57 + 12r + 3d + x). Record 0 collects new steps; $1C5B pushes it
into the queue, performs record 1 ($1CD8: $1E39, $1DF2, $1EC4, $1E86) and shifts the queue down.

Delayed movement queue: 11 records of 4 step counters (one per direction) x 3 actors, interleaved
(counter d of record r for actor x at actor_move_queue + 12r + 3d + x). Record 0 collects new steps;
actor_action_step pushes it into the queue, performs record 1 (actor_undo_up_loop: actor_move_down,
actor_move_up, actor_move_right, actor_move_left) and shifts the queue down. draw_room clears it.

Per-character flag: nonzero = the pose was already picked in this update (set by $2785, $1F8D, $2B65,
cleared by $1C68).

Per-actor flag: nonzero = the pose was already picked in this update (set by select_actor_pose, actor_set_idle
and apply_fight_hits, cleared by actor_action_run).

Collected-lantern effect slots (3): timer (0 = free, counts up; $3228 draws the steps at 8, 12, 16, 20),
column and text line of the lantern (set by $306B).

Burst trap slots (3): timer (0 = free; touch_trap_tile starts it at 1, update_burst_traps counts it up and draws
the burst at 8, 12, 16 and 20 and frees the slot at 24), column - 1 and text line - 1 of the trap
(set by touch_trap_tile).
255 bytes that no code reads or writes (they hold a copy of older code and data).

Char row address tables (24 entries): entry r = screen row r+1. char_row_screen_lo/hi = $8C28 + 40r,
char_row_colour_hi with the same low byte = colour RAM $D828 + 40r. Used by set_char_row_pointers.

Char row address tables (24 entries): entry r = screen row r+1. char_row_screen_lo/hi = $8C28 + 40r
(game_screen + 40 + 40r), char_row_colour_hi with the same low byte = colour RAM $D828 + 40r.
Used by set_char_row_pointers.

Start-up builder of the character animation frames (called once by the cold start at $04F0).
First it loops forever unless $CF8F and $CFAF both hold $B9 (bytes of the $CF00 block).
Then for each pair of frame numbers X = $D1, $CF, ... 1 (odd) and X-1 (even): frame X is expanded to its address,
which for odd frames is the buffer $CAE0 (when its address high byte $1239,X is 0 the buffer is cleared instead);
frame X-1 is expanded to its own address ($1167/$1239) and the buffer is ORed into it. So each even frame =
its own shape + the odd shape. $51 holds the frame number.
Frame format: 96 bytes = 3 columns of 32 rows, column after column; each source pixel becomes a %11
multicolour pixel. Ends with JMP $0080 (an RTS).

Start-up builder of the background contact masks, called once by cold_start after the room charsets are
expanded. First it loops for ever unless prot_signature_a = $B9 and prot_signature_b = prot_signature_a
(protection key page).
Then for each pair of frame numbers X = $D1, $CF, ... 1 (odd) and X-1 (even): frame X is expanded into the
96-byte buffer shift_mask_col0 ($CAE0; the odd entries of frame_gfx_addr_lo/hi point there), or the buffer is

Room maps, one per room 0-19 (pointer tables $4B34 lo / $4B49 hi, indexed by room $29), decoded by $0AD7 in
the room drawer at $09BC. Each map is a run-length stream of 440 tiles = 11 rows of 40 tiles, drawn from screen row 3:
  c = $01-$7F: repeat the next byte c times;
  c = $81-$FF: copy the next c-$80 bytes;
  c = $80: end of the map.
(c = $00 would repeat 256 times; no map uses it.) A tile is 2 characters high: bits 0-6 = character n on the upper
screen row, n+$80 on the row below. Bit 7 set = the tile's colour RAM becomes $F8 (multicolour, black) instead of the
room colour from $47A0. The charset is chosen by room: rooms 0-9 $A000, 10-17 and 19 $A800, 18 $B000.
$3CA7 writes $80 to the first byte of rooms 0, 1 and 5 when the byte at $0000 is not $EF, which empties them.

Protection key page, bytes $CF00-$CF78 that no protection check reads (the checks read only $CF79-$CFBA).
WHAT: not data. The bytes run in blocks of 32: $CF00-$CF1F mostly $FF, $CF20-$CF3F mostly $00, $CF40-$CF5F mostly
$FF, $CF60-$CF78 mostly $00, and the tail $CFC0-$CFDF $FF / $CFE0-$CFFF $00 continues the same 64-byte period.
29 of the 190 unread bytes have stray bits ($BF $C0 $F5 $EE $C6 $F6 in the $FF blocks; $A7 $07 $02 $FF $B7 in the $00
blocks), and some come back at the same offset in each 64-byte period ($02 $FF at $CF2A-$CF2B, $CF6A-$CF6B, $CFEA-$CFEB).
This is the typical power-on content of C64 DRAM, not a disk sector, a table or random data: no byte sequence
matches the game, no checksum relation to the key bytes was found, the content does not decode as code or text.
WHERE: the cracked file carries the page at file offset $A700; the SSG mover copies it to $CF00.
Origin: unknown. It is uninitialised RAM of the machine on which the key page was made: the original loader wrote
the 64 key bytes $CF79-$CFB8 into a page whose other bytes were never written. Whether that machine was the
cracker's (key built at load time) or the publisher's (page saved whole) the bytes cannot tell. Not development
build material.

Not a leftover: the game's own bytes are here (see src/). The 66 key bytes $CF79-$CFBA that the protection checks read (src/protection_key_page.asm). $CFB9-$CFBA are 0, as the $CFA0-$CFBF block of the power-on pattern would be.
